choice: F = S * exp(r * T) with r = 6.5%, not the previous day's parity forward
reason: Parity forwards from settlement prices scatter by 10 to 20 points around the theoretical basis on short contracts; on expiry day the theoretical basis is under 6 points and goes to zero.

choice: Main floor 5 minutes; sensitivity with 60 and 120 minutes and with an 'Asian' clock that ends at 15:10
reason: The last anchor is 15:00 (30 minutes left), so a 5-minute floor never binds. The official close is a 15:00 to 15:30 average, whose variance equals that of a single price at about 15:10.

choice: Before 10:15 the 60-minute lag is the RV since 09:15 scaled to 60 minutes
reason: Spilling into the previous afternoon would mix in the overnight gap and, from 3 Aug 2026, the closing-auction jump.

choice: From 3 Aug 2026 outcome windows must end by 15:14
reason: The 1-minute index is frozen from 15:15 to about 15:28 and then jumps to the auction close.

choice: Net GEX at spot divided by gross GEX at the previous close (a day constant known before the open)
reason: A signed quantity has no logarithm; dividing by a pre-open day constant makes days with very different OI comparable without using any information from the day itself.

choice: Only OI changes; today's implied vols are kept (interpolated at the placebo strikes)
reason: The placebo is meant to break the link to the real OI profile, not to change the volatility smile.

choice: Another day's profile is moved by a whole number of 50-point strikes so that its previous-close forward sits on today's
reason: Keeping strikes on the real 50-point grid means a pure round-number effect would survive the placebo, while the real OI shape is lost.

topic: leverage control (added after the first run)
choice: Robustness specs that add the signed and the absolute index move since the previous close
reason: Under the US convention net GEX at spot is call gamma minus put gamma, which rises mechanically when the index rises (calls sit above, puts below); volatility falls after rises (the leverage effect). Without this control a signed coefficient can reflect the leverage effect, not hedging. The headline specification was kept exactly as pre-specified.

topic: expiry afternoon placebos (added after the first run)
choice: Placebos (a), (b) and (c) are also run on the expiry afternoon subsample (13:00 to 15:00)
reason: The first run showed a positive secondary coefficient there; a placebo is the natural check of whether it is specific to the real OI profile.
